Take half of the coefficient of x and square it (*(–b/2a)²*), add/subtract it to complete the square. Write the right side as a binomial squared plus/subtracted value, factor, and solve roots!

Stationary points occur where *f'(x) = 0* or is undefined (critical points). Find the derivative: e.g., for *y=3x³–4x²*, derive to *9x²–8x*. Set it equal to zero (*9x²–8x=0*), factor: *x(9x–8)=0*, so x=0 or *x=8/9*. Verify using second derivative test (e.g., plug into *36x–8*—positive means minimum, negative max).
